title: Solar Storm!
description: The Sun just released a burst of energetic particles. They will reach your spacecraft within hours and can damage sensitive detectors.

options.label: Enter safe mode
options.description: Switch the instruments off and point the arrays at the Sun until the storm passes (3 days without science).
options.explanation: Safe mode protected the instruments. Three days of lost data is a small price compared with a damaged detector.

options.label: Keep observing
options.description: Keep collecting data and trust the shielding.
options.explanation: Lucky! The storm passed without damage and you kept collecting data.
options.badExplanation: A particle strike damaged a detector. Science output is permanently reduced by 30%.

title: Micrometeoroid Strike
description: A dust grain smaller than a grain of sand hit a solar panel at 10 km/s. The panel now gives 10% less power.

options.label: Reduce instrument use
options.description: Run instruments 15% less so the battery always stays charged.
options.explanation: Cutting the load kept the power budget positive. Engineers keep margins for exactly this.

options.label: Keep full operations
options.description: Keep everything on and accept deeper battery drain.
options.explanation: Your power margin absorbed the hit; full operations continued.
options.badExplanation: Without enough power margin the battery ran flat in the shadow. The spacecraft rebooted and lost 10 days of science.

title: Ground Station Outage
description: A storm over the ground station (or urgent maintenance) means no contact for 3 days. Data will pile up in onboard memory.

options.label: Rent backup antenna time
options.description: $1.5M to use a partner agency's antenna.
options.explanation: Renting backup time kept the data flowing. Real missions sign backup agreements for this reason.

options.label: Wait it out
options.description: Store data onboard for 3 days.
options.explanation: Memory held the data until contact returned (if your memory was big enough).

title: Reaction Wheel Failure
description: One of the reaction wheels that turn the spacecraft has stopped spinning.

options.label: Switch to the spare wheel
options.description: Larger buses carry a backup wheel.
options.explanation: The spare took over. Carrying a backup (redundancy) saved the mission's pointing.

options.label: Get help from magnetorquers
options.description: Use Earth's magnetic field to assist (near Earth only). Pointing 5× worse.
options.explanation: The magnetorquers hold the spacecraft steady, but less precisely.

options.label: Accept degraded pointing
options.description: Pointing 20× worse; precise instruments will blur.
options.explanation: The spacecraft wobbles more now, so sharp instruments lose quality.

title: Budget Cut!
description: Government funding was reduced. Finance asks your mission to give back 10% of its budget.

options.label: Pay from our reserve
options.description: Give back 10% of the budget from the money you kept in reserve.
options.explanation: Your reserve absorbed the cut. That is exactly why planners keep one.

options.label: End the mission one year early
options.description: Stop operations a year early to save operations money.
options.explanation: Ending early saves operations money but costs a year of science.

options.label: Switch to a cheaper ground network
options.description: Move to the next cheaper ground network.
options.explanation: Cheaper ground stations save money but give fewer contact hours, so less data comes home.

title: Computer Reset
description: A cosmic ray flipped a bit in the computer's memory and it rebooted.
autoHandledText: A cosmic ray flipped a bit in memory, but the rad-hard computer fixed it automatically. No science lost.

options.label: Reload software from the ground
options.description: Send the flight software up again (1 day of science and contact lost).
options.explanation: The team reloaded the software; one day of science was lost.

options.label: Upload a protective patch
options.description: $0.5M for a patch that adds memory error checking (2 days of science lost).
options.explanation: The patch adds memory error checking, so this will not happen again.

title: Space Debris Close Approach
description: Tracking shows a piece of old rocket debris may pass within 200 metres of your spacecraft in 12 hours.

options.label: Perform an avoidance burn
options.description: Fire the thrusters for a 2 m/s dodge (1 day of science lost).
options.explanation: A 2 m/s burn moved you safely aside. Operators perform thousands of these every year.

options.label: Stay on course
options.description: Trust the odds and keep observing.
options.explanation: The debris passed by. The odds were low, but not zero.
options.badExplanation: The debris hit the spacecraft. The mission is over, and the collision created even more debris.

title: Unexpected Discovery!
description: Your instruments spotted something unexpected: an unusual signal worth a closer look.

options.label: Follow up and send extra data
options.description: Point the instruments at the signal for 5 days; it triples the data you make.
options.explanation: The follow-up produced a bonus result. Flexible plans let missions chase surprises (if your downlink can handle the extra data).

options.label: Stick to the schedule
options.description: Keep the planned observing schedule.
options.explanation: Routine continued. Safe, but the surprise stays a mystery.

title: Global Dust Storm on Mars
description: A planet-wide dust storm is spreading across Mars. Rovers lose sunlight and go quiet, but the atmosphere is doing something scientists rarely see.

options.label: Observe the storm
options.description: Turn every instrument to the storm for 30 days; relay traffic halves.
options.explanation: Your orbiter recorded the storm from above: a rare dataset. The rovers were sending less anyway.

options.label: Focus on relay duty
options.description: Keep the relay channel ready for the rovers.
options.explanation: You kept the relay channel ready, but most rovers were asleep to save power.

title: Battery Wearing Out
description: After thousands of charge cycles the battery holds 20% less energy.

options.label: Switch off some instruments in eclipse
options.description: Run fewer instruments in the shadow (science −10%).
options.explanation: Saving power in the shadow protects the aging battery.

options.label: Keep everything on
options.description: Keep full operations and hope the battery lasts.
options.explanation: The battery still had enough capacity; operations continued.
options.badExplanation: The battery ran out in eclipse and the spacecraft spent 15 days in emergency safe mode.
